name: Sertraline
route_note: Oral tablets or oral concentrate once daily.

discovery.note: Developed from tametraline, an earlier Pfizer noradrenaline/dopamine uptake inhibitor; the cis-(1S,4S) enantiomer proved highly serotonin-selective.

tagline: Widely prescribed SSRI licensed for depression and a broad range of anxiety disorders
summary: Sertraline is an SSRI used for major depression and several anxiety disorders, including OCD, panic disorder, PTSD and social anxiety disorder. Introduced by Pfizer as Zoloft in 1991, it became one of the most prescribed antidepressants in the world.
mechanism: Sertraline potently and selectively inhibits the serotonin transporter, increasing synaptic serotonin. Compared with other SSRIs it has relatively greater affinity for the dopamine transporter and for sigma-1 receptors, although the clinical significance is uncertain.
As with other SSRIs, therapeutic effects emerge over several weeks, reflecting adaptive changes in serotonergic signalling rather than the acute increase in serotonin.
uses: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (adults and children aged 6 and over)

history.title: Synthesis
history.detail: Pfizer chemists Kenneth Koe and Willard Welch identify sertraline.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: The FDA approves Zoloft for depression in December 1991.

history.title: OCD in children
history.detail: Sertraline is approved for paediatric OCD, among the first SSRIs with a paediatric indication.

history.title: PTSD
history.detail: Sertraline becomes the first drug approved by the FDA for post-traumatic stress disorder.

history.title: Suicidality warning
history.detail: Class boxed warning on suicidality in young people is added to all antidepressants.

history.title: Generics
history.detail: US generic sertraline launches after patent expiry.

history.title: Viatris
history.detail: Zoloft passes to Viatris when Pfizer's Upjohn business merges with Mylan.

pk.metabolism: Hepatic N-demethylation via several CYPs (CYP2B6, 2C19, 3A4 and others)

safety.boxed_warning: Increased risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviours in children, adolescents and young adults (under 25) taking antidepressants; monitor for clinical worsening.

facts: Sertraline was the first medicine approved by the FDA for PTSD.
It is consistently among the most prescribed psychiatric drugs in the United States.
